purpose: Premium Visual, Motion Direction, Motion Runtime, Caption, Audio & Generative Layer. Load only after Operational Master + visual architecture are known.

authority.generativePixels: conceptual-or-illustrative-only; official and factual overlays remain deterministic

referenceDNA.rule: If the user supplies a visual/video reference, extract composition, hierarchy, color distribution, materiality, motion, transitions, typography, depth, camera, density, rhythm and evidence relationship. Translate principles into an original solution; never copy pixel coordinates, proprietary artwork or marketplace source templates.

styleSystem.rule: Every visual architecture has exactly three curated, materially distinct premium style directions.

templateKits.coverage: exactly three materially different directed kits for each of nine Production Masters
templateKits.rule: Prefer a matching executable Premium Template Kit over inventing a generic composition from scratch when the brief fits. Visual and temporal distinctness are both required.

materials.rule: Materials must support hierarchy, depth or continuity; do not add them merely as decoration.

motionLibrary.thirdPartyRule: license + provenance + deterministic smoke render required before production

motionDirection.rule: Use motion-direction knowledge after kit selection and before implementation. Upstream motion knowledge may improve craft but can never override the Design System, Brand Bridge, factual QA or rights/provenance.

transitions.rule: Use a coherent transition grammar to carry focus, state, material, depth or hierarchy. Do not use random transition packs; no logo/wave distortion.

captions.rule: Captions are deterministic, safe-area aware and phrase/block-led. Never shrink critical copy into microtext or bake captions into generative pixels.

lottie.externalAuthoringBridge: Lottie Creator MCP when actually connected in the user's MCP-capable client
lottie.rule: Use first-party Lotties freely under Design System roles. Third-party Lottie stays review-only until license/provenance, deterministic render, brand adaptation and visual QA pass.

audio.rule: Use only licensed, first-party or authorized audio. Synchronize to BPM when it helps, but factual reading time, voice clarity and narrative meaning override forced beat sync.

generativeVideo.statusRule: Only integrated-dry-run or integrated-live profiles may be invoked from this repository. adapter-candidate profiles are routing knowledge only until a governed adapter, current-doc revalidation and explicit credentials exist.
generativeVideo.preferredMode: image-to-video when an approved first frame can constrain composition
generativeVideo.rule: Use generative video only when it materially adds atmosphere, depth, explanation or continuity; final facts, captions and identity remain deterministic.

runtime.deterministic: Remotion + GSAP + Motion + SVG + first-party Lottie + first-party transitions + deterministic caption systems + optional rights-verified audio timing
runtime.motionDirection: CIAPACOV Motion Director + curated official upstream principles
runtime.generative: short governed conceptual clips assembled beneath deterministic identity/factual/caption overlays

selectionProtocol: 1. Keep the selected Operational Master and visual architecture; do not reopen the whole repository.
2. If a user reference exists, read reference-analysis-dimensions.json and extract its visual DNA without copying it.
3. Read only the single matching premium style preset record and present/use its three curated directions.
4. Select the closest matching executable directed Premium Template Kit from the same Production Master; do not collapse three kits into one layout with style swaps.
5. Load only the selected kit material IDs and motion IDs; all first-party premium materials and premium motion modules are executable.

6. For motion-heavy work, read claude/motion-direction.compact.json before implementation: resolve emotional intent, hero, setup→action→resolution, primary/secondary/ambient layers, timing/easing family, path anchoring and holds.

7. Consult claude/upstream-motion-intelligence.compact.json only if tool/authoring choice matters. Do not run remote npx installers blindly and do not confuse popularity, labs or external bridges with production integration.

8. Add first-party Lottie only where it serves a beat, state, route, data or utility purpose. External Lottie authoring via Creator MCP is optional and only real when the user's MCP-capable client is actually connected.
9. Select a coherent first-party transition grammar where scene handoffs need continuity; do not combine random transitions for novelty.
10. If subtitles/captions are required, choose one of the six governed caption systems and keep them inside the active Design System safe area.
11. If licensed/authorized audio exists, load only the selected Production Master's sound-design preset and optionally build a BPM frame grid. Silence is acceptable; rights-unknown audio is not.

12. If deterministic motion cannot efficiently deliver needed atmosphere/depth/explanation, choose one governed generative shot archetype. If provider choice matters, use the capability catalog/router; never confuse adapter-candidate with executable integration.
13. Prefer an approved first-frame image-to-video flow when composition continuity matters.
14. Keep all names, prices, routes, phone numbers, metrics, captions, logos and documentary evidence in deterministic layers.
15. Run anti-generic QA plus the creative benchmark; premium final must score at least 82 and have zero factual/readability blockers.
16. Verify that an intended motion composition actually changes meaningfully over time; static premium video templates are a QA failure even if they render.

17. Run factual QA, Design System safe areas, caption readability, overflow, audio rights/readiness and media readiness before export, then inspect the actual render and audio mix. Review timing at reduced playback speed when subtle easing/choreography defects remain.
